agree.reason: Accepting the staff science and offering trip logs and an app trial makes the ask credible, but a commissioner who trusts staff gets no reason to think three fish or a shorter season would bring the stock back to target.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief, but "it won't be none" turns two captains' conditional intent to sell into a near-certainty, and "I've never gotten back to 170" rests on the 155 and roughly 160 figures rather than a stated fact.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 32-trip, roughly $29,000 loss, but leaves out other strong derived figures: 41 of 70 is 59% versus 17% booking the same, the cumulative trips lost during the recovery, and the 70% of this season already booked.

right_comparison.reason: It sets the 2-fish cut against 3 fish or a shorter season and describes the 2016 drop-and-partial-recovery trend accurately, but gives no sense of how far the alternatives fall short of the cut's conservation effect.

qualification.reason: It honestly says it can't predict how many boats close, and the logs and next-season app trial are commitments staff could check, but there's no date for the logs and no stated test of whether three fish works.

objections.reason: It deals with the trust-the-staff objection by conceding the science and uses the 9% share well, but it doesn't answer the core objection that a 3-fish limit may not cut harvest enough.

fit.reason: At about 300 plain spoken words with a clear opening, ask and close, it fits a two-minute public-comment slot.
